label: This tape is a reconstruction.
Its teaching comes from real ministries' handbooks and booklets, 1993–1996.
Every reason in it was taught to real people.
You can stop it at any time.

admission.text: The more we fight against homosexual thoughts, the more intense they become.
admission.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality, rev. © 1995, printed p. 133 (PDF p. 141); NMAH.AC.1428 B2 F13

admission.text: They can't “just stop”. … the most difficult task of your entire life.
admission.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality, rev. © 1995, printed p. 133 (PDF p. 141): 'leaving the gay lifestyle and the gay orientation may be the most difficult task of your entire life'

sentences.text: This teaching asked people to forget their music, their friends, their places.
sentences.source: Handbook rev. 1995: 'What Do We Lose?' (music, clothing, bars, the scene), printed p. 132; 'cut off relationships', p. 133; 'returning to old haunts … the old associations that music brings forth', p. 135

sentences.text: To guard every thought that went in, keep a journal, and report each week.
sentences.source: Handbook rev. 1995, printed pp. 130–131 ('It is our responsibility…'; workbook question 4, 'protecting your mind'); Steps Out class manual (Love in Action, c. 1994), p. iii ('KEEP A JOURNAL!', 'TAKE NOTES at each session', 'Spend time each week reflecting on last week's session. Share at the next meeting')

sentences.text: It made their families the cause.
sentences.source: Handbook rev. 1995, printed p. 13: 'the deepest root of homosexuality is a break in the relational bonds within the family'; Exodus booklet PR-02 (1993), printed pp. 7, 9, 13

sentences.text: When it did not work, it told them the failure was theirs.
sentences.source: Handbook rev. 1995, printed p. 130 ('This places the burden directly on us'), pp. 132–133 (the ambivalent: 'no permanent home in our minds'), p. 135 ('when an ex-gay person stumbles'; 'a feeling of failure')

sentences.text: It was written for pastors, counselors and lay workers.
sentences.source: Handbook rev. 1995, cover (PDF p. 2): 'A handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers'
